title: D4, D5 and D2 bite
description: User story under REQ-174 for DEFINE step 3 PR 6 (spec section 4 rows for D4, D5 and standards citation). D4 reports closed-set and ownerRef resolution as findings (stories:closedSets, stories:ownerRefResolves). D5 ships the concern catalogue module and the crosscut:catalogue check that enumerates applicable (reqShape, concern) pairs per in-scope REQ against the concern ledger. D2 ships skeleton:standardsCited that fails any registered standards pack that is neither cited in a REQ rationale or an ADR nor waived by a concern-ledger entry with key standards:<pack>. D5 is ackable: --check crosscut rides the same --ack fold as D3, exits 4 on an unacknowledged D5 failure at the current hash and 0 when acked at the current hash. Validate adds no finding for a missing AC class marker (decision 10 kept; the validate finding rows land in PR 8).
iWant: D4 to flag enumeration cues without a closed set, D5 to drive the eight-concern catalogue against the concern ledger for every REQ in scope, D2 to insist every registered standards pack is cited or waived, and --check crosscut to honour the recorded override at the current hash
soThat: an AC that invites unlisted values, an unresolved ownerRef, a REQ that forgot a crosscut concern or a registered standards pack that no document cites blocks the gate until the tree is fixed or the gate is acknowledged

acceptanceCriteria.description: [failure] given an AC "status is one of the following" with no bracketed list and no ownerRef, when D4 runs, then stories:closedSets fails it.

[happy] given an ownerRef { tacId, field: "interfaces[loan]" } resolving on that TAC, when D4 runs, then stories:ownerRefResolves passes; given interfaces[missing], then it fails with "ownerRef does not resolve". (PR 9 R11: ownerRef resolves on any existing field path, bracket grammar -- interfaces[<name>], responsibilities[<n>], dependencies[<name>], alternativesConsidered[<n>] -- or a bare schema field name -- purpose, decision, internalStructure, etc.; interfaces[loan] still resolves, interfaces[missing] still fails.)
[happy] given a persistence REQ with retention applied and timeAndTimezone waived with a reason, when D5 runs, then crosscut:catalogue passes it.
[failure] given an httpApi REQ with no errorEnvelope entry, when D5 runs, then crosscut:catalogue fails <REQ>:errorEnvelope.

[happy] (R8 2026-10-05) given a registered standards pack cited in an ADR, when D2 runs, then skeleton:standardsCited passes; uncited and unwaived, it fails standards:<pack>; given a concern-ledger entry concern 'standards:<pack>' with disposition 'applied' or 'waived', it passes (the check question reads 'cited, applied or waived').
[must-not] given a story with no class marker on any AC, when rcf define validate runs, then no finding is raised for the missing marker.

[happy] (PR 9 R11) given an ownerRef { tacId, field: "responsibilities[0]" } naming an existing responsibility index on that TAC, when D4 runs, then stories:ownerRefResolves passes; a bare field name (purpose, internalStructure, decision) resolves when the owning doc carries a non-empty value under that key.

[must-not] (PR 9 R11) given an ownerRef whose field uses dotted grammar (interfaces.loan, responsibilities.audit), when D4 or rcf define validate runs, then it fails with the finding naming the dotted field so the author can rewrite to bracket grammar.

[happy] (R7 2026-10-05) given a D2 scope narrowed so no REQ, PRD, TAD or brief statement is in scope but a registered standards pack is neither cited nor waived tree-wide, when D2 runs, then skeleton:standardsCited fails standards:<pack> and the stage state is failing (not notApplicable); the shared tree-wide-before-scope helper (ADR-4138) governs the ordering.
